I don’t know of any LinkedIn groups on this topic but I am part of two Slack channels – WriterHangout and Top of the Funnel – that you can join for free where you might be able to get some insights from other writers about this. 

I used to work in academia, so I know trying to get SMEs (aka academics) to do anything is like herding a bunch of cats. A few pieces of advice that I have used in the past that might be helpful (likely things you’re already doing)…

- Create a very clear system for the workflow that is distilled into as few steps as possible
- Use that workflow every single time, so it becomes a systematic review 
- Try asking SMEs for very specific feedback about their content rather than a general review and keep those asks very short and upfront in the requests you send 
- Give deadlines that say something to the effect of “Please respond with any updates by [DATE]. If I don’t hear from you, I will assume that you are happy with the content as it is today.” Giving them an out to not respond and you to be able to move forward has worked very well for me in the past. It actually makes people respond (somewhat counterintuitive). 
- I don’t know your process, but if it’s possible, I would update the content on your own and get feedback on the new content with a deadline request like the one outlined above. This narrows down the number of times you have to go to the SME for feedback. 

Ok, that’s all I can think of at the moment. I don’t know if you need any actual writing help or strategy assistance to think through how to rework the existing content, but I do have some bandwidth if you’re looking for another person to come on board to assist. Just let me know!
